definition: The smallest particle of an element, consisting of a nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons in shells.
clues: This is the building block of matter
It has a nucleus and electrons
It is the smallest part of an element
The smallest unit of an element — protons and neutrons form the nucleus, electrons orbit in shells

definition: The small, dense, positive core of an atom containing protons and neutrons. Diameter ~10⁻¹⁴ m; about 1/10,000 of the atom's diameter.
clues: This is the centre of an atom
It is very small and dense compared to the whole atom
It contains protons and neutrons
The dense, positive core of an atom — about 1/10,000 the diameter of the atom, but contains almost all of its mass

definition: The spontaneous and random emission of radiation from the unstable nucleus of an atom.
clues: This is a property of some atomic nuclei
It is spontaneous and random
It involves the nucleus emitting radiation
The random, spontaneous emission of radiation from an unstable nucleus — cannot be predicted or controlled by external conditions

definition: A particle emitted in alpha decay consisting of 2 protons and 2 neutrons (identical to a helium-4 nucleus). Charge: +2. Heavily ionising, stopped by paper.
clues: This is a type of nuclear radiation
It consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons
It is the most ionising but least penetrating type
A helium-4 nucleus emitted from a large unstable nucleus — highly ionising, stopped by paper or a few cm of air

definition: A fast-moving electron emitted from the nucleus when a neutron turns into a proton. Charge: −1. Moderately ionising, stopped by a few mm of aluminium.
clues: This is a type of nuclear radiation
It is a fast-moving electron from the nucleus
A neutron becomes a proton when this is emitted
A high-speed electron from the nucleus — moderately ionising, stopped by a few mm of aluminium or about 1 m of air

definition: Electromagnetic radiation emitted from the nucleus after alpha or beta decay. No mass or charge. Weakly ionising, stopped by thick lead or metres of concrete.
clues: This is a type of nuclear radiation
It is an electromagnetic wave with no mass or charge
It is the most penetrating type of radiation
A high-energy EM wave emitted from the nucleus — least ionising, most penetrating; stopped by thick lead or concrete

definition: The process by which radiation removes electrons from atoms, creating ions. Alpha particles cause the most ionisation; gamma rays the least.
clues: This is a process caused by nuclear radiation
It involves removing electrons from atoms
Alpha particles cause the most of this
Radiation knocking electrons off atoms to form ions — alpha particles are most ionising, gamma rays least; ionisation can damage living cells

definition: The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay. A fixed value for any given isotope, unaffected by external conditions.
clues: This is a property of radioactive isotopes
It is the time for half the atoms to decay
It is unaffected by temperature or pressure
The time for half the undecayed nuclei in a sample to decay — a constant for each isotope, used in carbon dating and safety planning

definition: The number of nuclear decays per second in a radioactive sample. Measured in becquerels (Bq). Decreases over time as nuclei decay.
clues: This is a property of radioactive samples
It is measured in becquerels
It decreases over time as the sample decays
The number of decays per second — measured in Bq; falls exponentially as the number of undecayed nuclei decreases

definition: The SI unit of radioactive activity. 1 Bq = 1 decay per second.
clues: This is a unit of measurement in nuclear physics
It is the unit of radioactive activity
1 of these equals 1 nuclear decay per second
The SI unit for radioactive decay rate — 1 Bq = 1 disintegration per second; named after Henri Becquerel

definition: The low-level radiation always present in the environment, from natural sources (radon gas, cosmic rays, rocks) and artificial sources (medical, nuclear industry).
clues: This is radiation that is always present in the environment
It comes from natural and artificial sources
Radon gas is the largest natural source in the UK
Constant low-level radiation from the environment — mainly from radon gas, cosmic rays, food and rocks; must be accounted for in experiments

definition: The splitting of a large, unstable nucleus (e.g. uranium-235) into two smaller nuclei when it absorbs a neutron, releasing large amounts of energy and more neutrons.
clues: This is a nuclear process that releases energy
A large nucleus splits into two smaller ones
It releases neutrons that can cause further reactions
A large nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits — releasing huge energy and more neutrons that can trigger a chain reaction

definition: A self-sustaining reaction where neutrons released by fission cause further fission reactions. Controlled in nuclear reactors; uncontrolled in nuclear weapons.
clues: This is a type of reaction in nuclear physics
Each reaction triggers more reactions
It is controlled in power stations and uncontrolled in bombs
Neutrons from one fission event trigger further fissions — controlled in reactors to produce steady power, uncontrolled in weapons

definition: The joining of two small nuclei (e.g. hydrogen isotopes) to form a larger nucleus, releasing large amounts of energy. Requires extremely high temperatures.
clues: This is a nuclear process that releases energy
Two small nuclei join together
It requires extremely high temperatures
Two light nuclei fuse into one heavier nucleus — releasing enormous energy; the process that powers stars, including the Sun

definition: A device that uses controlled nuclear fission to generate heat, which is used to produce steam to drive turbines and generate electricity.
clues: This is a device that generates electricity
It uses controlled nuclear fission
Heat produces steam which drives turbines
A controlled fission reactor — neutrons split uranium nuclei, releasing heat to make steam, which drives turbines to generate electricity

definition: The presence of radioactive material on or inside an object, person or surface when it should not be there.
clues: This is a radiation hazard
It involves radioactive material being where it shouldn't be
It can be internal or external
Unwanted radioactive material on or inside a person or object — the source is touching the body and could decay there

definition: Exposure to radiation from a source outside the body. The person does not become radioactive — they are just exposed to the radiation.
clues: This is a type of radiation exposure
The radiation source is outside the body
The exposed person does not become radioactive
Exposure to radiation from an external source — the body is exposed but not contaminated; ends when you move away from the source

definition: A nuclear equation showing the change in atomic number and mass number during alpha or beta decay.
clues: This is a type of equation in nuclear physics
It shows what happens to protons and neutrons during decay
The mass number and atomic number are both conserved
An equation showing nuclear changes during decay — mass numbers and atomic numbers balance on both sides

definition: A technique for dating organic materials by measuring the remaining proportion of radioactive carbon-14, which decays with a half-life of about 5,700 years.
clues: This is a technique for dating ancient materials
It uses a radioactive isotope of carbon
The half-life of this isotope is about 5700 years
Comparing the ratio of C-14 to C-12 in ancient organic material — the known half-life of C-14 allows age to be calculated

definition: A measure of the risk of harm from exposure to radiation, taking into account both the amount and type of radiation received. Measured in sieverts (Sv).
clues: This is a measure of radiation risk to the body
It takes into account the type of radiation
It is measured in sieverts
A measure combining radiation amount and type to estimate harm — measured in sieverts; used to set safe exposure limits

definition: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom. Also called the atomic number. Determines which element the atom belongs to.
clues: This is a property of an atom's nucleus
It defines which element an atom is
It is also called the atomic number
The count of protons in the nucleus — unique to each element; also equals the number of electrons in a neutral atom

definition: The number of neutrons in the nucleus of an atom. Calculated as mass number minus proton number.
clues: This is a property of an atom's nucleus
It can be calculated from two other values
It differs between isotopes of the same element
The number of neutrons in the nucleus — mass number minus atomic number; isotopes differ in this value
